meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Bijural: private law within Quebec is governed by the Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c CCQ-1991, civil law tradition); public law, criminal law, and federal statutes (including the Canada Business Corporations Act for federal entities) are governed by Common Law. Federal and provincial statutes coexist under the division of powers in the Constitution Act, 1867.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), in force July 1, 2020
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applied since September 21, 2017
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force December 30, 2018
Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement, in force April 1, 2021
Canada-European Free Trade Association (EFTA) Free Trade Agreement, in force July 1, 2009
Canada-China Foreign Investment Protection Agreement (FIPA), in force October 1, 2014
Canada-United States Tax Convention (signed September 26, 1980, as amended by Protocols through 2005) and the Canada-Quebec network of over 90 bilateral income tax treaties

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and its Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46 (ss 462.31 and 83.05-83.3); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17 (SEMA); United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 10; Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1 (Division VIII, Register of Individuals with Significant Control); Quebec Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 (obligation to transmit the register of persons having control to the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44 (ss 21.1-21.4, federal significant-control register, effective January 22, 2024, per Bill C-42); FINTRAC interpretive guidance and Global Affairs Canada sanctions administration.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificat de constitution) issued upon conclusive registration of the proposed articles of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille - Canada acceded to the HCCH 1961 Apostille Convention on June 29, 2023, in force domestically since January 11, 2024

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Quebec Name Search Report (Rapport de recherche de nom) prepared by an authorized research agent and tendered with the articles of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Designated nonexclusive name research agent operating under contract with the Ministre des Finances du Quebec, or REQ-approved search provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the report is to be used in a jurisdiction party to the 1961 Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized identification and due-diligence dossier of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO), comprising passport copy, proof of residential address, source of funds declaration, and personal history declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioned lawyer in the UBO's country of origin or Quebec notary for residents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention state) or Consular Legalization (non-Convention state), plus sworn translation into French/English where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for incorporation filer and registered agent (Pouvoir / Mandat pour constitution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary at the place of signature, with legalization chain where signed outside Canada
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, with French or English certified translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the draft articles of incorporation and by-laws (Statuts constitutifs et reglements internes) bearing the signature of founding shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec notary or business law firm drafting the constitutional documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization where the document is submitted to foreign banking, payment-rail (Stripe, Paddle), or corporate-group KYC

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of every proposed incorporator, director, officer, and UBO against (i) the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (SEMA and Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act lists), (ii) the Canadian regulations derived from United Nations Security Council resolutions (United Nations Act), (iii) the Criminal Code s 83.05 lists, and (iv) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, given that the target payment rails (Stripe Billing and Paddle) are United States processors subject to US sanctions enforcement and may impose independent financial-institution screening. Where any person is a Politically Exposed Person (Canadian or foreign, or a family member or close associate), the application requires written senior-management approval, enhanced ongoing monitoring, reasonable source-of-funds verification, and FINTRAC-compliant record keeping for at least five years. All screening results must be documented in the pre-incorporation AML/CFT file, dated, and signed by the responsible compliance officer or registered agent.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - online incorporation and name-search portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca); federal alternative for a CBCA business corporation: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (https://www.ic.gc.ca/eic/site/065.nsf/eng/home) - under the federal route the NUANS name reservation is valid for 90 days, whereas the provincial Quebec name search report is valid for 60 days
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Quebec corporate names are mandatory in French under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, and the Regulation respecting the language of commerce and business, CQLR c C-11, r 9. The corporate name must contain a compulsory French designation (e.g., 'Societe par actions', 'Compagnie', 'Inc.', 'Corp.') and must not contain an English-only complement; a registered trademark exemption is available for a name that is the exact registered trademark and whose French presence is absent only to preserve the mark. Transliteration: names are registered in Latin script using standard French orthography, with no statutory Chinese, Cyrillic, or non-Latin transliteration register; any trade name used in a foreign language requires a French version filed for legal-publicity purposes.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank/banque, trust, insurance/assurance, loan company - requires prior approval of the Autorite des marches financiers (AMF)
University/universite, college, institute of technology - requires approval of the Ministere de l'Enseignement superieur
Lawyer/avocat, notary/notaire, auditor, engineer/ingenieur, chartered professional accountant (CPA), physician/medecin - requires approval of the applicable professional order
Royal/Royale, Crown, Canada, Quebec, federal, provincial, municipal, ministere - connotes public authority and requires prior ministerial or Crown consent
Police, security service, investigator, detective - regulated or misleading markers subject to sector approval
Commission, court, tribunal, office de la langue, ombudsman - implies a governmental body and is systematically refused
Holding, group, global, international or other deceptive broad descriptive terms lacking factual support from the proposed activities
Expletives, discriminatory terms, or words contrary to public order (bonnes moeurs) - refused per the Civil Code of Quebec public-order rules
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Step 1: Upon refusal, REQ issues a written notice stating the legal motive for rejection. Step 2: The applicant (or its Quebec counsel/notary) must within 45 days submit a corrected name proposal, obtain a fresh name search report (valid 60 days), and file an amended application for incorporation; repeated refusals require a distinct alternative name rather than a mere appeal. Step 3: Where the registraire has rejected a name on grounds the applicant disputes, the applicant may within 30 days of notification apply to the Court of Quebec (Cour du Quebec) for judicial review under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, and may simultaneously apply to the court for a provisional order directing the registraire to reserve the disputed name pending review. Step 4: For a federal CBCA name refusal, the applicant may request reconsideration by Corporations Canada within 30 days, then seek judicial review before the Federal Court under section 14 of the Canada Business Corporations Act. Step 5: Legal counsel's parallel SOP includes verifying the trademark register (Canadian Intellectual Property Office) and Quebec business-name register prior to refiling, so that the remedial filing avoids identical or 'confusingly similar' obstacles.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for the ISIC 6201 low-code website-builder industry, provided the office is a physical address in Quebec where legal process, REQ correspondence, and Revenu Quebec documents can be served during business hours. Under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and the Quebec Business Corporations Act, the registered office (siege social) may be the office of a licensed corporate agent or a commercial virtual-office provider with dedicated mail reception and a named person authorized to accept service; there is no statutory requirement of a storefront, inventory, or employee occupancy for a purely digital software publisher. Practical limitation: the address cannot be a bare post-office box and must correspond to an actual civic address; CRA and Revenu Quebec generally accept a virtual-office address for a low-risk software vendor, while the company must maintain complete corporate records and, for GST/QST purposes, a books-and-records address in Canada. Recommended structure for this client: a Quebec registered office at the corporate agent's commercial address coupled with a director's home address as the business address for ordinary correspondence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, quantified at approximately 5% probability per compliance year. REQ performs predominantly documentary verifications of name, directors, UBO declarations, and annual declarations rather than unannounced visits, and unannounced on-site inspections occur primarily where third-party complaints or address-flagging of known mass virtual-office locations arise. Revenu Quebec and CRA field audits for a no-inventory, no-retail-space e-commerce software company are typically desk-based (GST/QST reconciliation, corporate income tax review, payroll accounts if any), with an on-site audit risk arising only in cases of persistent non-filing, excessive input-tax-credit claims, or evidence of unreported offshore revenue. The residual 5% risk is managed by maintaining a professional virtual-office reception capable of receiving and time-stamping any process or inspector communication.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Quebec corporate name search report (Rapport de recherche de nom) through an authorized research agent, including verification against the REQ register and Canadian trademark database
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized Quebec name-search agent (private provider contractually mandated by the Ministere des Finances du Quebec)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory market tariff of approximately CAD 25-50 per standard report; USD equivalent at 1.38 CAD/USD, excluding rush handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the corporation and issuance of the certificate of incorporation (Constitution d'une societe par actions) via the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec electronic filing system, including the opening of the legal-publicity dossier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory incorporation fee of CAD 337 for electronic filing (2024 REQ tariff); USD equivalent at 1.38 CAD/USD; no registered capital or minimum-capital levy applies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: French-language compliance review of the corporate name, by-laws, and standard contracts (Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec business-law firm or language-law compliance consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of CAD 150-250 flat fee for a single low-risk software entity; statutory certification not otherwise levied

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and statutory agent services for the first year, comprising Quebec domestic address, reception of legal process, and forwarding of REQ/Revenu Quebec mail
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Quebec corporate-services provider (virtual office and registered agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of CAD 400-700 per year for a low-risk non-regulated ISIC 6201 corporation; USD equivalent at 1.38 CAD/USD

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Full pre-incorporation legal services bundle: drafting and notarization review of articles of incorporation, by-laws, organizational resolutions, UBO and significant-control register creation, minute book initialization, AML/KYB policy, and submission of all filings
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market flat fee of CAD 900-1,400 for a single-shareholder, single-UBO, no-license software corporation; USD equivalent at 1.38 CAD/USD

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the UBO identification dossier and the power of attorney for incorporation filing (passport, proof of address, source-of-funds declaration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary of the country of signature (foreign notary for non-resident UBOs) or Quebec notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Quebec notarial tariff of approximately CAD 100-150 per identification bundle, plus applicable foreign notarial charges; USD equivalent displayed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Authentication and apostille of the pre-incorporation document bundle (name search report, certificate of incorporation, UBO dossier, power of attorney, certified by-laws) for use in foreign banking and payment-rail KYC
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministere des Relations internationales et de la Francophonie du Quebec (MRIF) for provincial documents, or Global Affairs Canada authentication services for federal documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory authentication fee of approximately CAD 15-45 per document (MRIF/GAC 2024 tariff); five documents included in this line at the low end of the range

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Annual PEP, OFAC, UN, and Canadian autonomous sanctions screening subscription covering all directors, officers, UBOs, and associated natural persons, with quarterly refresh
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial AML compliance data provider (FINTRAC-compliant screening software)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market subscription benchmark of CAD 150-250 per year for a single low-risk entity integrated with the registered agent's compliance workflow

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of federal (CRA GST/Business Number) and Quebec (Revenu Quebec QST) tax accounts, and attestation of no prior criminal or tax-consent impediment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory service provided without fee; expenses limited to postage and any incidental courier, which are waived in this estimate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1 (Loi sur les societes par actions), sections 1-78, 86, 98-121 (articles, registered office, directors, share capital); complementary provisions of the Civil Code of Quebec (CCQ-1991) arts. 296-472
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), an agency of the Ministere du Travail, de l'Emploi et de la Solidarite sociale
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution) - Form AR-1B, filed electronically via the Registraire's secured online portal or by paper submission to 2050 rue Bleury, Montreal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; articles must specify at least one class of shares with rights and restrictions; no escrow account or capital deposit required; unpaid share capital is not permitted to be represented as paid
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscription agreements presented to this Board for shares of the Corporation be and are hereby accepted and the subscribers are registered as shareholders of record. FURTHER RESOLVED that the Corporation adopt as its head office and registered office the address at ---- in the City of ----, Province of Quebec, and that the books and records of the Corporation be maintained there. FURTHER RESOLVED that the persons named in the appointment schedule be and are hereby elected as directors, and that ---- be appointed Chief Executive Officer and ---- Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until removed by resolution. FURTHER RESOLVED that banking resolutions, signing authorities, and the corporate seal be established as per the attached schedule.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Notice of Constitutional Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (online name search and reservation module)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a Quebec Distinctiveness Search (previously NUANS) via a licensed search house or directly through the Registraire portal. File a Name Reservation Request (Demande de reservation de nom) with up to three proposed names. If a numbered company is preferred, a legal name in form '1234567 Canada Inc.' is automatically assigned by the Registrar upon filing of the Articles.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application
NUANS/Distinctiveness Search report (not older than 90 days)
Proof of payment of name reservation fee
Consent of any third party named in the proposed corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or flagged as confusing, file a revised name reservation within 15 days; alternatively proceed as a numbered company and subsequently apply for a change of name under s. 19 LSA once the incorporation is complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - Corporate Registry Division (online incorporation service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic Articles of Incorporation form in the Registraire's online system or submit paper Form AR-1B. Include the corporation's name, share structure (class A common voting, class B non-voting as needed), restrictions on transfer, number and qualifications of directors, and the registered office address. The incorporators (may be one or more individuals aged 18+ or bodies corporate) must execute the articles. Pay the prescribed fee by credit card or electronic funds transfer.
required_dossiers: Completed Articles of Incorporation (AR-1B)
Name reservation certificate (if a named corporation is used)
Declaration of incorporators (addresses and signatures)
Fee payment receipt
Power of attorney if filed through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency notice (avis de traitement), remedy the inconsistent clauses within 30 days by filing amended articles through the same portal; if the filing is legally incomplete, withdraw and re-file with a fresh fee within the same payment period where a credit is available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation (Certificat de constitution) and assigns the nine-digit Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). The company's constitutive record is automatically entered into the Register of Enterprises. Download the certificate and the official notice of publication from the Registraire's portal; store them in the company's golden book.
required_dossiers: Approved Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of Incorporation (issued by Registrar)
Notice of registration with NEQ number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not delivered within SLA, request a search of the enterprise register and contact the Registrar's client service; any clerical error in the certificate may be corrected by a 'Rectification' request filed under s. 24 LSA within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution and Governance Organization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors of the Corporation (internal governance act; no external filing required, but minutes must be kept at the registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of directors after incorporation. Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution: accept share subscriptions, approve share issuances, elect officers, designate the registered office, approve the corporate seal, execute banking resolutions, and authorize the opening of corporate bank accounts with sanctioned signing officers. Document all resolutions in the minute book and distribute share certificates to shareholders.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution (minutes of directors)
Share subscription and register of shareholders
Share certificates signed by directors
Registered office address notice
Banking resolution and authorized signatory list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any shareholder or director dissents, record the dissent in minutes and re-vote under s. 118 LSA; if the officer appointments are invalidated, hold an emergency board meeting to ratify the appointment; deficiencies in share issuance must be corrected by a supplementary share issue resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Revenue Quebec and Federal Tax Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenue Quebec (Revenu Quebec), Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the new company for a Quebec tax account and corporate income tax file via Revenue Quebec's online service (Clic Revenu), using the NEQ and corporation number. Also register the company with CRA for a federal corporate income tax account, GST/QST harmonization (if applicable), and payroll deductions if employees are hired. Provide the registered office address and lists of directors.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NEQ registration notice
Corporation income tax registration form (Revenue Quebec and CRA)
GST/HST and QST registration applications (if annual taxable revenue exceeds CAD 30,000)
Payroll account application (PD27 / RC159) or appointment of authorized agents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed or rejected due to missing directors' SIN/identification numbers, submit a written rectification to Revenue Quebec and CRA within 21 days; retroactive registration dates may be requested with supporting incorporation certificate evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Registers, Registered Office Signage, and Compliance Posting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors and Corporate Secretary (internal compliance; municipal inspection by the local borough for signage permits)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and maintain the statutory registers: register of shareholders, register of directors, register of share transfers, and minute book as required under ss. 23, 88, 99 LSA. Ensure physical signage identifying the company is posted at the registered office if required by the local municipality, and post any mandatory notices (e.g., safety and health posters) at the workplace. Renew the annual updating declaration to the Registrar before the anniversary of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Minute book and registers
Certificate of Incorporation displayed or filed as municipal requirement
Municipal signage permit (if the building by-law requires it)
Annual declaration reminder notice from the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If annual updating declaration is missed, file it immediately with late fee and apply for reinstatement under s. 289 LSA; if the register is incomplete, reconstruct it from available records and sign a rectification minute.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministere de l'Economie, de l'Innovation et de l'Energie (MEIE) and Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) - software sector has no mandatory industrial operating license
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - ISIC 6201 (software publishing and web application services) is not a regulated or licensed industrial activity in Quebec; no specific operating permit or sectoral authorization is required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) - Direction de l'evaluation environnementale
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the activity constitutes an office-based software service with no industrial construction, no waste discharge, no land disturbance, and no groundwater or surface water intake; no EIA filing or environmental authorization certificate (certificat d'autorisation) is required under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c Q-2, s. 22 and 31.1
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None applicable for core operations. Office premises must comply with municipal wastewater discharge by-laws if the building is connected to municipal sewers; electronic waste (computers, servers, peripherals) must be recycled under the RECYC-QUEBEC extended producer responsibility program (Plan de gestion des residus); records must demonstrate absence of any regulated contaminant emissions (alkanes, VOCs, or refrigerants) from operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the local municipal fire safety service after inspection of the leased or owned office space; compliance certificate for structural load and safe exit routes required by the Regie du batiment du Quebec (RBQ) for any commercial occupancy not covered by a grandfathered license; workplace safety registration with the Commission des normes, de l'equite, de la sante et de la securite du travail (CNESST) if any employee is hired, along with the mandatory prevention program and safety signage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec, portals at canada.ca/cra and revenuquebec.gouv.qc.ca
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities obtain Business Number (BN) from CRA via online portal or Form RC59; Quebec entities register with Revenu Québec for QST number upon meeting threshold
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections; hybrid mismatch rules under Income Tax Act apply

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory GST/QST registration; electronic filing via CRA and Revenu Québec portals; real-time digital reporting through GST/HST e-services with QR code invoicing

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% GST/QST rate for goods exported from Canada or services supplied to non-residents; requires proof of export and non-resident recipient status
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties up to 200% of tax due; retrospective adjustments with interest; criminal prosecution for willful fraud

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administering cross-border currency reporting and anti-money laundering supervision. Canada does not maintain a dedicated foreign exchange administration or exchange-control authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange controls, surrender requirements, or central bank approvals for inbound investment or profit remittance. Non-resident corporate shareholders face Part XIII withholding tax on dividends and certain payments, generally 25% unless reduced by treaty, but no convertibility hurdle exists. Capital repatriation and loan repayments are freely permitted provided they correspond to documented equity or debt instruments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts in Canada. Exporters may hold, convert, or repatriate foreign currency proceeds freely. Cross-border monetary transfers equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000 are reportable to FINTRAC, and records supporting export transactions must be retained for tax and audit purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate to High viability for using licensed Payment Service Providers and Electronic Money Institutions as ancillary collection/settlement rails, but low viability as the sole treasury platform. Offshore EMIs lacking Canadian Money Services Business (MSB) registration with FINTRAC are legally restricted from maintaining domestic accounts or clearing CAD in the Large Value Transfer System. A Quebec-based MSB registration and provincial licensing under the Retail Payment Activities Act may be required, making Tier 1 banks mandatory for core corporate treasury functions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and authorized signatories are not universally required to attend a branch in person; most Tier 1 Canadian banks permit fully remote corporate onboarding using video KYC, digital identity verification, and electronic signatures for low-risk software companies. Nevertheless, a live video compliance interview remains mandatory in practice, and some banks may require physical appearance for non-resident directors or complex ownership structures. Notarized corporate documents, board resolutions, and beneficial ownership attestations must be provided in either case.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate ownership and foreign parent jurisdiction as a sanctioned or high-risk territory
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation, register of directors, share register with beneficial ownership schedule, corporate chart, audited financial statements, tax residence certificates, and a board resolution identifying economic substance, business purpose, and source of initial funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk product description or perceived mismatch between no-code website builder activity and banking treasury flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial SaaS license agreement, website/application demo, customer contract samples, payment processor agreements (Stripe, Paddle), and a written business narrative demonstrating standardized recurring SaaS revenue rather than high-risk or unlicensed activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or rapid cross-border wire activity from multi-jurisdictional customer and vendor bases
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed transaction ledger, source-of-funds and purpose-of-payment documentation per counterparty, customer due diligence files, invoices and contracts, foreign exchange hedging documentation, and a treasury policy demonstrating predictable and explainable cash-flow patterns.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections should be structured as either share-subscription proceeds or documented shareholder loans. Routing is via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign parent or investor bank to the Quebec entity's Tier 1 bank account, with a clear remittance narrative distinguishing 'share capital contribution' or 'intercompany loan disbursement'. Canada has no statutory payment-purpose code system; however, FINTRAC large-transaction reporting applies to receipts equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000. The receiving bank will require verification of source of funds, and non-Canadian investors may need to file under the Investment Canada Act only if thresholds are exceeded; standard verification include a board resolution, share subscription agreement, loan agreement, and evidence of the remitter's corporate existence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound operational disbursements for SaaS vendors, contractors, and licensing fees are cleared using SWIFT MT103 cross-border wires, with Canadian domestic settlements executed through the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS). For procurement of physical goods ancillary to software business, Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credits) may be used. Payments to OFAC, UN, and Canadian sanctions targets are prohibited, and outgoing wires of CAD 10,000 or more trigger FINTRAC reporting. Beneficiary bank details and SWIFT BIC/IBAN equivalents must be reconciled against bank records to prevent sanctions-related delays.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers reminder notices; repeated failure to file for one or more years may lead to administrative dissolution under the Canada Business Corporations Act. Reinstatement requires payment of prescribed fees and filing of all omitted returns.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary date of enterprise registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file leads to late fees, suspension of the registration, and eventual administrative dissolution or cancellation of the enterprise by the Registrar. Reinstatement requires filing the declaration, paying penalties, and obtaining a certificate of rehabilitation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax, plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; compound interest on outstanding balances; directors may be liable for unremitted source deductions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty and compounded interest on tax due; repeated non-filing may result in arbitrary assessment, administrative penalties, and forced filing by Revenu Québec.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A non-distributing CBCA or Québec Business Corporations Act corporation must appoint an independent auditor unless all shareholders unanimously consent in writing or by resolution to dispense with the auditor for that fiscal year. Public or distributing corporations are subject to a mandatory independent audit. There is no revenue threshold exemption under CBCA or QBCA for private corporations; the unanimous consent exemption is the applicable criterion.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian public companies must prepare financial statements in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). Private corporations in Quebec may use IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) of CPA Canada. For income tax filings, accounting income is reconciled to taxable income under the Income Tax Act and applicable Quebec tax legislation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate federal or Quebec government annual UBO filing exists. Under the CBCA, a private corporation must maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) and update it within 15 days after any change. Share transfers are recorded in the securities register; directors and officers are confirmed annually through the federal annual return and the Quebec annual declaration. Beneficial shareholding details are not reported to the government unless administratively requested.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book containing shareholders' and directors' minutes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000–22,000 per year for a privately held Quebec corporation preparing ASPE financial statements; the range increases with IFRS conversion, interprovincial registrations, consolidation, or complex revenue transactions typical of a no-code SaaS business.
